objective_for_doctor: A 8-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a fever, pain that improves when you lean forward, and a knife stroke pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi. I have a fever and my throat hurts a lot—like a sharp “knife-stroke” pain in my tonsils and the back of my mouth. It gets better when I lean forward, but it hurts to swallow, my voice is hoarse, and I’m having trouble breathing. Also, I’m making more saliva than usual.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—can you tell me when these symptoms started and whether you have any drooling, muffled “hot potato” voice, or trouble opening your mouth?  
Doctor: Also, do you have a cough, runny nose, or any one-sided throat swelling?

It started pretty fast—like within a few hours. Yes, I’m drooling more than usual. My voice is hoarse, but I don’t know if it’s “hot potato”—it just sounds different. I can open my mouth, but the throat pain is very bad.

I don’t have a cough or runny nose. I also don’t know about one-sided swelling—I feel pain on both sides of my tonsils.

Doctor: I’m concerned about a deep throat infection—could you check if swallowing is impossible (can you manage liquids), and do you have a high fever/does breathing feel worse when lying flat?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any neck swelling or stiffness, and has your temperature been measured (number)?

I can swallow liquids, but it’s really hard and it hurts a lot—so it feels almost impossible because of the pain. My breathing feels very bad, but I’m not sure about whether it gets worse when I lie flat.

I don’t know about neck swelling or stiffness. My temperature has been measured, but I don’t have the number with me.

Doctor: I’m going to examine your throat and neck now—can you sit up, open wide, and stick your tongue out; also, is your breathing noisy (like a high-pitched sound) or are you struggling to swallow your own saliva?  
Doctor: While we do that, I need a quick answer: do you have a rash or severe headache/neck stiffness, and can you report your highest measured temperature number if you can find it?

I can sit up and open wide. I can stick my tongue out, and I’m struggling because it hurts, but I’ll try.

My breathing feels hard and fast, and I am swallowing my saliva a lot because I feel like I can’t keep up. No rash that I know of, and I don’t know about severe headache or neck stiffness. I don’t have the highest temperature number with me.

Doctor: Your drooling, very fast onset sore throat with “knife-stroke” pain that improves leaning forward, hoarseness, and worsening breathing/stridor raise concern for a deep neck infection (especially peritonsillar/parapharyngeal abscess); I’m going to request urgent tests to confirm and guide treatment—REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff; REQUEST TEST: Neck_CT_with_contrast_or_neck_ultrasound.  
Doctor: While we wait, can you tell me if your breathing is noisy/high-pitched (stridor) and whether the uvula or tonsil area looks shifted to one side on your exam (even if it’s hard to tell)?  
Doctor: If you’re having significant breathing difficulty, you need immediate ER care—stay sitting upright and don’t eat or drink.  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Suspected deep neck space infection—peritonsillar/parapharyngeal abscess (needs urgent imaging and IV antibiotics)
